class TestCompletionItem(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests for CompletionItem class."""

    def test_init_default_values(self):
        """Test CompletionItem with default values."""
        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
        
        item = CompletionItem("test_value")
        self.assertEqual(item.value, "test_value")
        self.assertEqual(item.type, "plain")
        self.assertIsNone(item.help)

    def test_init_with_all_params(self):
        """Test CompletionItem with all parameters."""
        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
        
        item = CompletionItem("value", type="file", help="A file option")
        self.assertEqual(item.value, "value")
        self.assertEqual(item.type, "file")
        self.assertEqual(item.help, "A file option")

    def test_getattr_returns_info(self):
        """Test __getattr__ returns metadata from kwargs."""
        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
        
        item = CompletionItem("val", custom_attr="custom_value")
        self.assertEqual(item.custom_attr, "custom_value")

    def test_getattr_returns_none_for_missing(self):
        """Test __getattr__ returns None for missing attributes."""
        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
        
        item = CompletionItem("val")
        self.assertIsNone(item.nonexistent)

    def test_slots_attribute_access(self):
        """Test that slots work correctly."""
        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
        
        item = CompletionItem("test")
        # Should be able to access value, type, help
        _ = item.value
        _ = item.type
        _ = item.help


class TestShellCompleteBase(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests for ShellComplete base class."""

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures."""
        from click import Command
        
        self.cli = Command("test_cli")
        self.ctx_args = {}
        self.prog_name = "test_prog"
        self.complete_var = "TEST_COMPLETE"

    def test_init_sets_attributes(self):
        """Test __init__ sets all attributes."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, self.prog_name, self.complete_var)
        self.assertEqual(comp.cli, self.cli)
        self.assertEqual(comp.ctx_args, self.ctx_args)
        self.assertEqual(comp.prog_name, self.prog_name)
        self.assertEqual(comp.complete_var, self.complete_var)

    def test_func_name_property(self):
        """Test func_name property generates correct name."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, "my-prog", self.complete_var)
        self.assertIn("_my_prog_completion", comp.func_name)

    def test_func_name_with_underscores(self):
        """Test func_name handles underscores in prog_name."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, "my_prog", self.complete_var)
        self.assertIn("_my_prog_completion", comp.func_name)

    def test_source_vars(self):
        """Test source_vars returns expected dict."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, "prog", self.complete_var)
        vars_dict = comp.source_vars()
        self.assertIn("complete_func", vars_dict)
        self.assertIn("complete_var", vars_dict)
        self.assertIn("prog_name", vars_dict)
        self.assertEqual(vars_dict["complete_var"], self.complete_var)
        self.assertEqual(vars_dict["prog_name"], "prog")

    def test_source_raises_notimplemented(self):
        """Test source method raises error when no template."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, "prog", self.complete_var)
        with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
            comp.source()

    def test_get_completion_args_raises_notimplemented(self):
        """Test get_completion_args raises NotImplementedError."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, "prog", self.complete_var)
        with self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError):
            comp.get_completion_args()

    def test_format_completion_raises_notimplemented(self):
        """Test format_completion raises NotImplementedError."""
        from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
        from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem
        
        comp = ShellComplete(self.cli, self.ctx_args, "prog", self.complete_var)
        item = CompletionItem("test")
        with self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError):
            comp.format_completion(item)

        retrieved = get_completion_class("renamed")
        self.assertEqual(retrieved, CustomComplete)

class TestIsIncompleteArgument(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests for _is_incomplete_argument function."""

    def test_non_argument_param(self):
        """Test returns False for non-Argument parameter."""
        from click import Option, Context
        from click.shell_completion import _is_incomplete_argument
        
        param = Option(["--test"])
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        result = _is_incomplete_argument(ctx, param)
        self.assertFalse(result)

    def test_nargs_negative_one(self):
        """Test returns True when nargs is -1."""
        from click import Argument, Context
        from click.shell_completion import _is_incomplete_argument
        
        param = Argument(["name"], nargs=-1)
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        ctx.params = {"name": []}
        ctx.get_parameter_source.return_value = mock.MagicMock()
        result = _is_incomplete_argument(ctx, param)
        self.assertTrue(result)

    def test_commandline_source(self):
        """Test returns False when source is COMMANDLINE and nargs > 1 filled."""
        from click import Argument, Context, ParameterSource
        from click.shell_completion import _is_incomplete_argument
        
        param = Argument(["name"], nargs=2)
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        ctx.params = {"name": ("a", "b")}
        ctx.get_parameter_source.return_value = ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE
        result = _is_incomplete_argument(ctx, param)
        self.assertFalse(result)

class TestResolveIncomplete(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests for _resolve_incomplete function."""

    def test_option_start_completion(self):
        """Test returning command for option name completion."""
        from click import Command, Context
        from click.shell_completion import _resolve_incomplete
        
        cli = Command("test_cli")
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        ctx.command = cli
        ctx._opt_prefixes = ["-", "--"]
        ctx.help_option_names = ["--help", "-h"]
        
        args = []
        incomplete = "--option"
        result_obj, result_incomplete = _resolve_incomplete(ctx, args, incomplete)
        self.assertEqual(result_obj, cli)
        self.assertEqual(result_incomplete, "--option")

    def test_equals_sign_handling(self):
        """Test handling of equals sign in incomplete."""
        from click import Command, Context
        from click.shell_completion import _resolve_incomplete
        
        cli = Command("test_cli")
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        ctx.command = cli
        ctx._opt_prefixes = ["-", "--"]
        ctx.help_option_names = ["--help", "-h"]
        
        args = []
        incomplete = "="
        result_obj, result_incomplete = _resolve_incomplete(ctx, args, incomplete)
        self.assertEqual(result_incomplete, "")

    def test_equals_in_option(self):
        """Test handling of = in option name."""
        from click import Command, Context
        from click.shell_completion import _resolve_incomplete
        
        cli = Command("test_cli")
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        ctx.command = cli
        ctx._opt_prefixes = ["-", "--"]
        ctx.help_option_names = ["--help", "-h"]
        
        args = []
        incomplete = "--option=value"
        result_obj, result_incomplete = _resolve_incomplete(ctx, args, incomplete)
        self.assertIn("--option", args)
        self.assertEqual(result_incomplete, "value")

    def test_double_dash_stops_options(self):
        """Test that -- stops option treatment."""
        from click import Command, Context
        from click.shell_completion import _resolve_incomplete
        
        cli = Command("test_cli")
        ctx = mock.MagicMock(spec=Context)
        ctx.command = cli
        ctx._opt_prefixes = ["-", "--"]
        ctx.help_option_names = ["--help", "-h"]
        type(ctx.command).get_params = mock.MagicMock(return_value=[])
        
        args = ["--"]

class MockRequest:

        new_req = MockRequest()

        new_req.body = self.body

        import tempfile

        # Create a temporary netrc file
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', delete=False, suffix='.netrc') as f:
            f.write("machine example.com login testuser password testpass\n")
            temp_netrc = f.name
        
        try:
            old_netrc = os.environ.get('NETRC')
            os.environ['NETRC'] = temp_netrc
            result = get_netrc_auth("http://example.com/path")
            # Result should be a tuple or None (depending on netrc parsing)
            if result is not None:
                assert isinstance(result, tuple)
        finally:
            os.unlink(temp_netrc)
            if old_netrc is not None:
                os.environ['NETRC'] = old_netrc
            elif 'NETRC' in os.environ:
                del os.environ['NETRC']

class TestConfigFromEnvvar:
    """Tests for Config.from_envvar"""

    def test_from_envvar_success(self, monkeypatch):
        from flask.config import Config
        
        # Create a temp config file
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.py', delete=False) as f:
            f.write("DEBUG = True\nSECRET_KEY = 'test'\n")
            temp_file = f.name
        
        try:

            config = Config("/some/path")
            result = config.from_envvar("MY_SETTINGS")
            
            assert result is True
            assert config["DEBUG"] is True
            assert config["SECRET_KEY"] == "test"

            os.unlink(temp_file)

        config = Config("/some/path")

        config = Config("/some/path")

class TestIntegration:

    def test_full_workflow(self):
        from flask.config import Config
        
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            # Start with defaults
            config = Config(tmpdir, defaults={"DEFAULT_KEY": "default_value"})
            
            # Add more via from_mapping
            config.from_mapping(MAPPING_KEY="mapping_value")
            
            # Load from pyfile
            config_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, "config.py")
            with open(config_file, 'w') as f:
                f.write("FILE_KEY = 'file_value'\n")
            
            config.from_pyfile("config.py")
            
            # Verify all values
            assert config["DEFAULT_KEY"] == "default_value"
            assert config["MAPPING_KEY"] == "mapping_value"
            assert config["FILE_KEY"] == "file_value"

    def test_nested_prefixed_env_with_complex_structure(self, monkeypatch):
        from flask.config import Config
        
        monkeypatch.setenv("APP_DB__HOST", "localhost")
        monkeypatch.setenv("APP_DB__PORT", "5432")

        monkeypatch.setenv("APP_CACHE__ENABLED", "true")

    assert copied.min_width == original.min_width

    assert copied.ratio == original.ratio
    assert copied.no_wrap == original.no_wrap
    assert len(copied._cells) == 0  # Cells should be cleared

import pytest

class TestDefaultTemplateCtxProcessor:
    """Tests for _default_template_ctx_processor function."""
    
    def test_empty_context_no_app_or_request(self):
        """Test when neither app context nor request context exists."""
        from flask.templating import _default_template_ctx_processor
        
        result = _default_template_ctx_processor()
        assert result == {}
    
    def test_with_app_context_only(self):
        """Test with only app context available."""
        from flask.templating import _default_template_ctx_processor
        
        mock_appctx = Mock()
        mock_appctx.g = {"key": "value"}
        
        with patch('flask.templating._cv_app') as mock_cv_app, \
             patch('flask.templating._cv_request') as mock_cv_request:
            mock_cv_app.get.return_value = mock_appctx
            mock_cv_request.get.return_value = None
            
            result = _default_template_ctx_processor()
            assert 'g' in result
            assert result['g'] == {"key": "value"}
            assert 'request' not in result
            assert 'session' not in result
    
    def test_with_request_context_only(self):
        """Test with only request context available."""
        from flask.templating import _default_template_ctx_processor
        
        mock_reqctx = MagicMock()
        mock_reqctx.request = {"url": "http://test.com"}
        mock_reqctx.session = {"user": "testuser"}
        
        with patch('flask.templating._cv_app') as mock_cv_app, \
             patch('flask.templating._cv_request') as mock_cv_request:
            mock_cv_app.get.return_value = None
            mock_cv_request.get.return_value = mock_reqctx
            
            result = _default_template_ctx_processor()
            assert 'request' in result
            assert 'session' in result
            assert result['request'] == {"url": "http://test.com"}
            assert result['session'] == {"user": "testuser"}
            assert 'g' not in result
    
    def test_with_both_contexts(self):
        """Test with both app and request contexts available."""
        from flask.templating import _default_template_ctx_processor
        
        mock_appctx = MagicMock()
        mock_appctx.g = {"data": "app_data"}
        
        mock_reqctx = MagicMock()
        mock_reqctx.request = {"path": "/test"}
        mock_reqctx.session = {"id": 123}
        
        with patch('flask.templating._cv_app') as mock_cv_app, \
             patch('flask.templating._cv_request') as mock_cv_request:
            mock_cv_app.get.return_value = mock_appctx
            mock_cv_request.get.return_value = mock_reqctx
            
            result = _default_template_ctx_processor()
            assert 'g' in result
            assert 'request' in result
            assert 'session' in result
            assert result['g'] == {"data": "app_data"}
            assert result['request'] == {"path": "/test"}
            assert result['session'] == {"id": 123}

class TestTrackThread:
    """Tests for _TrackThread class."""
    
    def test_track_thread_init(self):
        """Test initialization of _TrackThread."""
        from rich.progress import Progress, _TrackThread
        
        progress = Progress()
        task_id = progress.add_task("test", total=10)
        
        thread = _TrackThread(progress, task_id, update_period=0.1)
        
        assert thread.progress is progress
        assert thread.task_id == task_id
        assert thread.update_period == 0.1
        assert isinstance(thread.done, Event)
        assert thread.completed == 0
        
        progress.stop()
        progress.live.stop()
    
    def test_track_thread_enter_exit(self):
        """Test context manager behavior of _TrackThread."""
        from rich.progress import Progress, _TrackThread
        
        progress = Progress(disable=True)
        task_id = progress.add_task("test", total=10)
        
        with _TrackThread(progress, task_id, update_period=0.1) as thread:
            assert thread.done.is_set() == False
        
        # After exit, done should be set
        assert thread.done.is_set() == True
        
        progress.stop()

        """Test open function in binary mode."""
        from rich.progress import open as progress_open
        
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', delete=False) as f:
            f.write(b"hello world")
            temp_path = f.name
        
        try:
            with progress_open(temp_path, mode='rb') as reader:
                data = reader.read()
                assert data == b"hello world"
        finally:
            os.unlink(temp_path)

        finally:

import pytest

class TestSyntaxTheme:
    """Tests for SyntaxTheme base class."""
    
    def test_get_style_for_token_not_implemented(self):
        """Test that get_style_for_token raises NotImplementedError."""
        from rich.syntax import SyntaxTheme
        
        # Create a concrete subclass to test abstract methods
        class ConcreteTheme(SyntaxTheme):
            def get_style_for_token(self, token_type):
                raise NotImplementedError("test")
            def get_background_style(self):
                raise NotImplementedError("test")
        
        theme = ConcreteTheme()
        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="test"):
            theme.get_style_for_token(Token)
    
    def test_get_background_style_not_implemented(self):
        """Test that get_background_style raises NotImplementedError."""
        from rich.syntax import SyntaxTheme
        
        # Create a concrete subclass to test abstract methods
        class ConcreteTheme(SyntaxTheme):
            def get_style_for_token(self, token_type):
                return None
            def get_background_style(self):
                raise NotImplementedError("test")
        
        theme = ConcreteTheme()
        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="test"):
            theme.get_background_style()


class TestPygmentsSyntaxTheme:
    """Tests for PygmentsSyntaxTheme class."""
    
    def test_init_with_string_theme(self):
        """Test initialization with string theme name."""
        from rich.syntax import PygmentsSyntaxTheme
        
        theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme("monokai")
        assert theme._pygments_style_class is not None
    
    def test_init_with_invalid_theme_fallback(self):
        """Test initialization falls back to default theme on invalid name."""
        from rich.syntax import PygmentsSyntaxTheme
        
        theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme("invalid_theme_name_12345")
        # Should fallback to "default" theme
        assert theme._pygments_style_class is not None
    
    def test_init_with_pygments_style_class(self):
        """Test initialization with Pygments style class."""
        from rich.syntax import PygmentsSyntaxTheme
        from pygments.styles import get_style_by_name
        
        style_class = get_style_by_name("emacs")
        theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme(style_class)
        assert theme._pygments_style_class == style_class
    
    def test_get_style_for_token_caching(self):
        """Test that styles are cached."""
        from rich.syntax import PygmentsSyntaxTheme
        
        theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme("monokai")
        style1 = theme.get_style_for_token(Token)
        style2 = theme.get_style_for_token(Token)
        assert style1 is style2  # Same object due to caching
    
    def test_get_style_for_token_keyerror_handling(self):
        """Test handling of KeyError in style lookup."""
        from rich.syntax import PygmentsSyntaxTheme
        
        theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme("monokai")
        # Unknown token type should return null style
        from rich.style import Style
        style = theme.get_style_for_token(("unknown", "token"))
        assert isinstance(style, Style)
    
    def test_get_background_style(self):
        """Test getting background style."""
        from rich.syntax import PygmentsSyntaxTheme

class TestMainBlockExecution:
    """Tests for if __name__ == '__main__' block execution."""

    def test_main_block_code_path(self):
        """Execute the main block code path using exec to cover those lines."""
        # This simulates running the file directly
        main_code = '''
from rich.console import Console

console = Console()
layout = Layout()

layout.split_column(
    Layout(name="header", size=3),
    Layout(ratio=1, name="main"),
    Layout(size=10, name="footer"),
)

layout["main"].split_row(Layout(name="side"), Layout(name="body", ratio=2))

layout["body"].split_row(Layout(name="content", ratio=2), Layout(name="s2"))

layout["s2"].split_column(
    Layout(name="top"), Layout(name="middle"), Layout(name="bottom")
)

layout["side"].split_column(Layout(layout.tree, name="left1"), Layout(name="left2"))

layout["content"].update("foo")

# Verify the structure was created correctly
assert layout.get("header") is not None
assert layout.get("main") is not None
assert layout.get("footer") is not None
assert layout.get("side") is not None
assert layout.get("body") is not None
assert layout.get("content") is not None
assert layout.get("s2") is not None
assert layout.get("top") is not None
assert layout.get("middle") is not None
assert layout.get("bottom") is not None
assert layout.get("left1") is not None
assert layout.get("left2") is not None
'''
        # Execute in a namespace that has the required imports
        namespace = {
            'Layout': __import__('rich.layout', fromlist=['Layout']).Layout,
            'Console': __import__('rich.console', fromlist=['Console']).Console,
        }
        exec(main_code, namespace)

    def test_main_block_via_reload(self):
        """Test by reloading the module with __name__ == '__main__'."""
        import importlib
        import sys
        
        # Get the layout module
        layout_module = sys.modules.get('rich.layout')
        
        # Save original __name__
        original_name = layout_module.__name__ if layout_module else None
        
        # Set __name__ to __main__ and reload
        if layout_module:
            layout_module.__name__ = '__main__'
            importlib.reload(layout_module)
            
            # Restore original name
            layout_module.__name__ = original_name

        def as_const(self, eval_ctx=None):
            from jinja2.nodes import get_eval_context, Impossible
            eval_ctx = get_eval_context(self, eval_ctx)
            f = lambda x: 1/0  # Always fails
            try:

                raise Impossible() from e

    def test_model_construct(self):

        class MyModel(BaseModel):
            name: str

        """Test model_copy method."""
        class MyModel(BaseModel):
            name: str
            age: int
        
        model1 = MyModel(name="Alice", age=28)
        model2 = model1.model_copy()
        assert model2.name == model1.name
        assert model2.age == model1.age
        assert model1 is not model2

    def test_model_copy_with_update(self):
        """Test model_copy with update parameter."""
        class MyModel(BaseModel):
            name: str
            age: int
        
        model1 = MyModel(name="Alice", age=28)
        model2 = model1.model_copy(update={"age": 30})
        assert model2.name == "Alice"
        assert model2.age == 30

        """Test model_copy with deep=True."""
        class Inner(BaseModel):
            value: int
        
        class Outer(BaseModel):
            inner: Inner
        
        outer1 = Outer(inner=Inner(value=1))
        outer2 = outer1.model_copy(deep=True)
        assert outer2.inner.value == outer1.inner.value
        assert outer2.inner is not outer1.inner

class TestUrlConstraints:
    """Tests for UrlConstraints class."""

    def test_url_constraints_hash(self):
        from pydantic.networks import UrlConstraints
        
        constraints = UrlConstraints(
            max_length=100,
            allowed_schemes=['http', 'https'],
            host_required=True,
            default_host='example.com',
            default_port=80,
            default_path='/api'
        )
        # Should be hashable
        h = hash(constraints)
        assert isinstance(h, int)

    def test_url_constraints_default_values(self):
        from pydantic.networks import UrlConstraints
        
        constraints = UrlConstraints()
        assert constraints.max_length is None
        assert constraints.allowed_schemes is None
        assert constraints.host_required is None
        assert constraints.default_host is None
        assert constraints.default_port is None
        assert constraints.default_path is None

    def test_url_constraints_with_all_params(self):
        from pydantic.networks import UrlConstraints
        
        constraints = UrlConstraints(
            max_length=500,
            allowed_schemes=['ftp', 'ftps'],
            host_required=False,
            default_host='default.example.com',
            default_port=21,
            default_path='/uploads'
        )
        assert constraints.max_length == 500
        assert constraints.allowed_schemes == ['ftp', 'ftps']
        assert constraints.host_required is False
        assert constraints.default_host == 'default.example.com'
        assert constraints.default_port == 21
        assert constraints.default_path == '/uploads'

    def test_url_constraints_different_hashes(self):
        from pydantic.networks import UrlConstraints
        
        c1 = UrlConstraints(max_length=100)
        c2 = UrlConstraints(max_length=200)
        assert hash(c1) != hash(c2)

    def test_url_constraints_same_values_same_hash(self):
        from pydantic.networks import UrlConstraints
        
        c1 = UrlConstraints(max_length=100, allowed_schemes=['http'])
        c2 = UrlConstraints(max_length=100, allowed_schemes=['http'])
        assert hash(c1) == hash(c2)

        from pydantic.networks import AnyUrl

"""Test suite for werkzeug.http module."""

import pytest
from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from hashlib import sha1


class TestQuoteHeaderValue:
    """Tests for quote_header_value function."""
    
    def test_quote_simple_token(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value("simple")
        assert result == "simple"
    
    def test_quote_with_spaces(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value("hello world")
        assert result == '"hello world"'
    
    def test_quote_empty_string(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value("")
        assert result == '""'
    
    def test_quote_with_quotes(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value('say "hello"')
        assert result == '"say \\"hello\\""'
    
    def test_quote_with_backslash(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value(r"path\to\file")
        assert result == '"path\\\\to\\\\file"'
    
    def test_allow_token_false(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value("simple", allow_token=False)
        assert result == '"simple"'
    
    def test_quote_number(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value(12345)
        assert result == "12345"
    
    def test_quote_special_chars(self):
        from werkzeug.http import quote_header_value
        result = quote_header_value("!#$%&'*+-.^`|~")
        assert result == "!#$%&'*+-.^`|~"


class TestUnquoteHeaderValue:
    """Tests for unquote_header_value function."""
    
    def test_unquote_quoted_value(self):
        from werkzeug.http import unquote_header_value
        result = unquote_header_value('"hello world"')
        assert result == "hello world"
    
    def test_unquote_escaped_quotes(self):
        from werkzeug.http import unquote_header_value
        result = unquote_header_value(r'"say \"hello\""')
        assert result == 'say "hello"'
    
    def test_unquote_escaped_backslashes(self):
        from werkzeug.http import unquote_header_value
        result = unquote_header_value(r'"path\\to\\file"')
        assert result == r"path\to\file"
    
    def test_unquote_unquoted_value(self):
        from werkzeug.http import unquote_header_value
        result = unquote_header_value("simple")
        assert result == "simple"
    
    def test_unquote_single_char(self):
        from werkzeug.http import unquote_header_value
        result = unquote_header_value('"a"')
        assert result == "a"


class TestDumpOptionsHeader:
    """Tests for dump_options_header function."""
    
    def test_basic_header(self):
        from werkzeug.http import dump_options_header
        result = dump_options_header("text/html", {"charset": "UTF-8"})
        assert result == "text/html; charset=UTF-8"
    
    def test_none_header(self):
        from werkzeug.http import dump_options_header
        result = dump_options_header(None, {"charset": "UTF-8"})
        assert result == "charset=UTF-8"
    
    def test_none_value_skipped(self):
        from werkzeug.http import dump_options_header
        result = dump_options_header("text/html", {"charset": None})
        assert result == "text/html"
    
    def test_multiple_options(self):
        from werkzeug.http import dump_options_header
        result = dump_options_header("text/html", {"charset": "UTF-8", "boundary": "abc"})
        assert "charset=UTF-8" in result
        assert "boundary=abc" in result
    
    def test_utf8_encoded_key(self):
        from werkzeug.http import dump_options_header
        result = dump_options_header("text/html", {"key*": "value"})
        assert "key*=value" in result

class TestDechunkedInput:

    def test_readable(self):

        import io
        
        mock_rfile = io.BytesIO(b"10\r\ndata\r\n")

    def test_read_chunk_len_valid(self):
        """Test reading valid chunk length."""
        from werkzeug.serving import DechunkedInput
        import io
        
        mock_rfile = io.BytesIO(b"10\r\ndata\r\n")
        di = DechunkedInput(mock_rfile)
        # Read the chunk header
        mock_rfile.readline = lambda: b"10\r\n"
        result = di.read_chunk_len()
        assert result == 16  # 0x10 in decimal

    def test_read_chunk_len_invalid(self):
        """Test reading invalid chunk length raises OSError."""
        from werkzeug.serving import DechunkedInput
        import io
        
        mock_rfile = io.BytesIO(b"invalid\r\ndata\r\n")
        di = DechunkedInput(mock_rfile)
        mock_rfile.readline = lambda: b"invalid\r\n"
        
        try:
            di.read_chunk_len()
            assert False, "Should have raised OSError"
        except OSError as e:
            assert "Invalid chunk header" in str(e)

    def test_read_chunk_len_negative(self):
        """Test reading negative chunk length raises OSError."""
        from werkzeug.serving import DechunkedInput
        import io
        
        mock_rfile = io.BytesIO(b"-10\r\ndata\r\n")
        di = DechunkedInput(mock_rfile)
        mock_rfile.readline = lambda: b"-10\r\n"
        
        try:
            di.read_chunk_len()
            assert False, "Should have raised OSError"
        except OSError as e:
            assert "Negative chunk length not allowed" in str(e)

    def test_readinto_consumes_data(self):
        """Test readinto properly consumes chunked data."""
        from werkzeug.serving import DechunkedInput
        import io
        
        # Create chunked data: 5 bytes "hello" followed by final chunk
        data = b"5\r\nhello\r\n0\r\n\r\n"
        mock_rfile = io.BytesIO(data)
        di = DechunkedInput(mock_rfile)
        
        buf = bytearray(100)
        n = di.readinto(buf)
        assert n == 5
        assert buf[:5] == b"hello"

        def app(environ, start_response):
            start_response('200 OK', [])
            return [b'']
        
        server = BaseWSGIServer("127.0.0.1", 0, app)

        import threading

        # The base class implementation may still do some logging but shouldn't crash

"""Test suite for werkzeug.routing.Map and MapAdapter classes."""

import pytest


class TestMapClass:
    """Tests for the Map class."""

    def test_map_init_with_rules(self):
        """Test Map initialization with rules."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        rule = Rule('/', endpoint='index')
        url_map = Map([rule])
        assert url_map is not None

    def test_map_init_empty(self):
        """Test Map initialization without rules."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map

        url_map = Map()
        assert url_map is not None

    def test_map_default_parameters(self):
        """Test Map default parameters."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map

        url_map = Map()
        assert url_map.strict_slashes is True
        assert url_map.merge_slashes is True
        assert url_map.redirect_defaults is True
        assert url_map.host_matching is False

    def test_map_custom_parameters(self):
        """Test Map with custom parameters."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map(
            rules=[],
            strict_slashes=False,
            merge_slashes=False,
            redirect_defaults=False,
            host_matching=True,
        )
        assert url_map.strict_slashes is False
        assert url_map.merge_slashes is False
        assert url_map.redirect_defaults is False
        assert url_map.host_matching is True

    def test_map_add_rule(self):
        """Test adding a rule to Map."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map()
        rule = Rule('/test', endpoint='test')
        url_map.add(rule)
        assert len(list(url_map.iter_rules())) == 1

    def test_map_iter_rules(self):
        """Test iterating over all rules."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index'), Rule('/about', endpoint='about')])
        rules = list(url_map.iter_rules())
        assert len(rules) == 2

    def test_map_iter_rules_by_endpoint(self):
        """Test iterating rules by endpoint."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([
            Rule('/', endpoint='index'),
            Rule('/about', endpoint='about'),
            Rule('/contact', endpoint='about'),
        ])
        about_rules = list(url_map.iter_rules('about'))
        assert len(about_rules) == 2

    def test_map_is_endpoint_expecting(self):
        """Test checking if endpoint expects arguments."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([
            Rule('/users/<int:id>', endpoint='user'),
            Rule('/users', endpoint='users_list'),
        ])
        assert url_map.is_endpoint_expecting('user', 'id') is True
        assert url_map.is_endpoint_expecting('user', 'name') is False
        assert url_map.is_endpoint_expecting('users_list', 'id') is False

    def test_map_bind(self):
        """Test binding Map to create MapAdapter."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        adapter = url_map.bind("example.com", "/")
        assert adapter is not None
        assert adapter.server_name == "example.com"

    def test_map_bind_to_environ(self):
        """Test binding Map to WSGI environ."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        environ = {
            'SERVER_NAME': 'example.com',
            'SERVER_PORT': '80',
            'PATH_INFO': '/',
            'REQUEST_METHOD': 'GET',
            'wsgi.url_scheme': 'http',
        }
        adapter = url_map.bind_to_environ(environ)
        assert adapter is not None

    def test_map_bind_host_matching_with_subdomain_raises(self):
        """Test that bind raises RuntimeError when host_matching and subdomain provided."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')], host_matching=True)
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
            url_map.bind("example.com", subdomain="www")

    def test_map_bind_invalid_server_name(self):
        """Test that bind raises BadHost for invalid server name."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule
        from werkzeug.exceptions import BadHost

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        # Use a non-ASCII character that will fail IDNA encoding
        with pytest.raises(BadHost):
            url_map.bind("münchen\x00.com")

    def test_map_update(self):
        """Test updating the map."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        url_map.update()
        # Should not raise any exception

    def test_map_repr(self):
        """Test Map repr."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        repr_str = repr(url_map)
        assert 'Map' in repr_str


class TestMapAdapterClass:
    """Tests for the MapAdapter class."""

    def test_match_simple_url(self):
        """Test matching a simple URL."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        adapter = url_map.bind("example.com", "/")
        endpoint, values = adapter.match("/")
        assert endpoint == 'index'
        assert values == {}

    def test_match_with_variable(self):
        """Test matching URL with variable."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/users/<int:id>', endpoint='user')])
        adapter = url_map.bind("example.com", "/")
        endpoint, values = adapter.match("/users/42")
        assert endpoint == 'user'
        assert values == {'id': 42}

    def test_match_with_string_variable(self):
        """Test matching URL with string variable."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule

        url_map = Map([Rule('/users/<name>', endpoint='user')])
        adapter = url_map.bind("example.com", "/")
        endpoint, values = adapter.match("/users/john")
        assert endpoint == 'user'
        assert values == {'name': 'john'}

        """Test matching non-existent URL raises NotFound."""
        from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule
        from werkzeug.exceptions import NotFound

        url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
        adapter = url_map.bind("example.com", "/")
        with pytest.raises(NotFound):
            adapter.match("/nonexistent")

        from werkzeug.exceptions import MethodNotAllowed

        adapter = url_map.bind("example.com", "/")

import pytest


class TestWeighting:
    """Tests for Weighting class."""

    def test_weighting_creation(self):
        from werkzeug.routing.rules import Weighting
        
        w = Weighting(1, [(0, 1)], 2, [3, 4])
        assert w.number_static_weights == 1
        assert w.static_weights == [(0, 1)]

class TestRequestApplication:
    """Tests for Request.application decorator."""

    def test_application_decorator(self):
        """Test application decorator wraps function."""
        from werkzeug.wrappers.request import Request

        @Request.application
        def app(request):
            return None

        # Should be callable
        assert callable(app)

    def test_application_closes_request(self):
        """Test that application closes request automatically."""
        from werkzeug.wrappers.request import Request

        closed = []

        class MockRequest(Request):
            def close(self):
                closed.append(True)
                super().close()

        @MockRequest.application
        def app(request):
            return lambda *args: b""

        # Call the decorated app
        environ = {
            "REQUEST_METHOD": "GET",
            "wsgi.url_scheme": "http",
            "SCRIPT_NAME": "",
            "PATH_INFO": "/",
            "QUERY_STRING": "",
            "CONTENT_TYPE": "",
            "wsgi.input": BytesIO(),
        }
        app(environ, lambda *args: b"")
        assert len(closed) > 0

"""Test suite for werkzeug.wsgi module."""

import io
import pytest


class TestResponder:
    """Tests for the responder decorator."""

    def test_responder_basic(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import responder

        @responder
        def app(environ, start_response):
            return lambda e, s: [b"Hello World"]

        environ = {"wsgi.url_scheme": "http", "SERVER_NAME": "localhost"}
        response = app(environ, lambda s, r: None)
        assert list(response) == [b"Hello World"]

    def test_responder_with_args(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import responder

        @responder
        def app(name, environ, start_response):
            return lambda e, s: [f"Hello {name}".encode()]

        environ = {"wsgi.url_scheme": "http", "SERVER_NAME": "localhost"}
        response = app("World", environ, lambda s, r: None)
        assert list(response) == [b"Hello World"]

class TestClosingIterator:
    """Tests for ClosingIterator class."""

    def test_closing_iterator_basic(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import ClosingIterator

        iterator = iter([b"hello", b" ", b"world"])
        closing = ClosingIterator(iterator)
        result = list(closing)
        assert result == [b"hello", b" ", b"world"]

    def test_closing_iterator_with_callback(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import ClosingIterator

        closed = []

        def cleanup():
            closed.append(True)

        iterator = iter([b"hello"])
        closing = ClosingIterator(iterator, cleanup)
        list(closing)
        closing.close()
        assert len(closed) == 1

    def test_closing_iterator_with_multiple_callbacks(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import ClosingIterator

        closed = []

        def cleanup1():
            closed.append(1)

        def cleanup2():
            closed.append(2)

        iterator = iter([b"hello"])
        closing = ClosingIterator(iterator, [cleanup1, cleanup2])
        list(closing)
        closing.close()
        assert sorted(closed) == [1, 2]

    def test_closing_iterator_iterable_has_close(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import ClosingIterator

        class CloseableIter:
            def __init__(self):
                self.closed = False

            def __iter__(self):
                return iter([b"hello"])

            def close(self):
                self.closed = True

        remaining = limited.exhaust()

        limited = LimitedStream(stream, limit=5)
        buf = bytearray(10)
        n = limited.readinto(buf)

        from werkzeug.exceptions import ClientDisconnected

        stream = io.BytesIO(b"")
        limited = LimitedStream(stream, limit=10, is_max=False)
        with pytest.raises(ClientDisconnected):
            limited.read(1)

    def test_limited_stream_readinto_error(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import LimitedStream
        from werkzeug.exceptions import ClientDisconnected

        class ErrorStream:
            def readinto(self, b):
                raise OSError("stream error")

        stream = ErrorStream()
        limited = LimitedStream(stream, limit=10)
        buf = bytearray(10)
        # When readinto raises an error, on_disconnect is called which raises ClientDisconnected
        with pytest.raises(ClientDisconnected):

    def test_limited_stream_read_error(self):
        from werkzeug.wsgi import LimitedStream
        from werkzeug.exceptions import ClientDisconnected

        class ErrorStream:

                raise ValueError("read error")

        stream = ErrorStream()
        limited = LimitedStream(stream, limit=10)
        buf = bytearray(10)
        # When read raises an error, on_disconnect is called which raises ClientDisconnected
        with pytest.raises(ClientDisconnected):
            limited.readinto(buf)
